sections.html:
Riverton is a city in Salt Lake County, in the southwestern corner of the Salt Lake Valley about 20 miles south and slightly west of Salt Lake City. It covers 12.58 square miles at 4,439 feet, and it borders South Jordan to the north, Draper to the east, Bluffdale to the south and Herriman to the west.

This is a different part of Utah from Orem, Provo and Pleasant Grove. Riverton is in Salt Lake County rather than Utah County, so its property tax, appeals and deed recording run through county offices in Salt Lake City, not Provo.

sections.h2: How did Riverton grow from a farm town to a suburb?
sections.html:
Riverton began as a farming community settled in the mid-1850s, probably first by Archibald Gardner, and it was originally called Gardnerville. Residents farmed alfalfa, wheat, sugar beets, tomatoes, poultry, sheep and dairy, and Jordan Valley Bank started as a community bank here in 1905.

Electricity arrived in 1912, and the Salt Lake and Utah Railroad (Orem Line) ran through town from 1914 to 1945. The city incorporated in the late 1940s. A 1996 annexation nearly doubled its size, and Herriman's incorporation in 2000 fixed the western boundary. Farm numbers in the county fell from 2,595 in 1950 to 798 in 1969. The old Riverton Elementary School became the Riverton Community Center and City Hall by 2005 to 2006.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Riverton housing?
sections.html:
Riverton is heavily owner-occupied, at 84.9% for 2020 to 2024. The Census Bureau counted 45,285 people in 2020, up 16.9% from 38,753 in 2010, and estimates 47,395 for July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: What neighborhoods and developments define Riverton?
sections.html:
Several of Riverton's named areas started as specific developments, and the city's records describe three of them.

  • Tithing Yard Hill is a residential planned development named for a former LDS tithing storage site.
  • Foothills was annexed in the 1980s, de-annexed after the developer's bankruptcy, and re-annexed in 1996.
  • Riverton City Park occupies the site of the former City Hall.

The city grew in pieces over time, so the year a house was built depends heavily on which part of Riverton it sits in.

sections.h2: How do you get around Riverton?
sections.html:
Riverton's main roads are Bangerter Highway, the Mountain View Corridor and Redwood Road, and drivers reach Interstate 15 through 12300 South or Bangerter Highway. Bangerter Highway (SR-154) enters Riverton as it curves north and crosses 13400 South, 12600 South and 11400 South, and the 12600 South interchange opened on May 19, 2022.

Transit is limited. UTA Route 126 started in April 2025 and runs hourly along 12600 South. Riverton workers average 24.8 minutes to work.

Riverton is in the Jordan School District, which also serves Bluffdale, Copperton, Herriman, South Jordan and most of West Jordan. The district had 57,866 students and 67 schools in 2021 to 2022 after the east-side communities left to form Canyons School District in 2009.

  • Elementary: Foothills, Midas Creek, Riverton, Rosamond, Rose Creek and Southland
  • Middle: Oquirrh Hills and South Hills
  • High: Riverton High School

Kauri Sue Hamilton School for special needs, the south campus of the Jordan Academy for Technology and Careers, and Saint Andrew Catholic School are also in Riverton. School boundaries do not match city limits, so many Riverton students attend schools in neighboring cities.

sections.h2: What jobs and services are close to Riverton homes?
sections.html:
Intermountain Riverton Hospital opened in November 2009 with a 24-hour emergency department, about 40 physician offices and a helicopter pad. It sits within the city limits.

Census figures show a median household income of $126,910 and an average of 3.30 people per household. With 84.9% of homes owner-occupied, a Riverton seller is usually selling a family house on a street where most neighbors are also owners.

sections.h2: What are Riverton's rules for accessory dwellings and short-term rentals?
sections.html:
Riverton's planning page now lists an accessory dwelling unit application and an owner-occupancy affidavit, submitted at City Hall, and short-term rentals go through a conditional use permit and an occupancy declaration. That was not always so: in October 2019 the city did not permit accessory dwellings and was drafting rules under state Senate Bill 34.

The 2019 draft proposed a 650 square foot limit, one parking space, an owner living on the property and one family in the unit. Residents argued the draft was too tight, and the council debated capping size at half the home instead. Check the city's current ordinance before you describe an apartment in a Riverton house as legal. The state ombudsman adds that cities may require a business license for short-term rentals but cannot act against someone only for listing a rental online.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for a Riverton house?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County assesses Riverton property, with a Notice of Valuation and Tax Change mailed in late July. The Board of Equalization accepts appeals from August 1 through September 15, and the deadline is 45 days from the notice or September 15, whichever is longer.

  • File online, by mail with form BE01, or in person at 2001 South State Street, Suite N3-300, Salt Lake City.
  • Include evidence, such as at least three comparable sales within the year before January 1, a signed settlement statement or a fee appraisal.
  • You can appeal only the total market value, not land or improvements separately.
  • The Board cannot change the tax you pay, only the valuation.

A hearing officer reviews the evidence, and the county reviews appeals around October 1 unless the State Tax Commission extends it. Taxes are due November 30 whether or not a decision has arrived. A further appeal goes to the Utah State Tax Commission within 30 days of the county decision. The appeals office can be reached at 385-468-7200.

sections.h2: Does earthquake risk matter when selling in Riverton?
sections.html:
It can come up. The Wasatch Fault is about 240 miles long, and the segment under Salt Lake City produced a major earthquake about 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. Magnitude 7 or larger quakes recur every 900 to 1,300 years on any one central segment, and a magnitude 5.7 quake on March 18, 2020, just north of Magna caused moderate damage.

Riverton's average annual precipitation is 15.76 inches, with winter snow and summers that occasionally top 100 degrees. A buyer's inspector may look at foundations and chimneys, and as-is sellers do not have to repair what an inspector finds.

sections.h2: What do Riverton sellers usually face, and how does a cash sale work?
sections.html:
Common situations in Riverton include an inherited family home, a house with a basement apartment that lacks paperwork, or a move on a short deadline. A cash sale to us follows a short path: you tell us about the property, we review it, and we make an offer based on condition.

We buy as-is, so you do not repair or stage. A title or escrow company handles the closing, and the deed is recorded with the county. Salt Lake County has its own recorder, so confirm recording details with your closing agent.

faqs.q: What county is Riverton, Utah in?
faqs.a: Riverton is in Salt Lake County, in the southwest corner of the Salt Lake Valley. Its property tax and appeals are handled by Salt Lake County, not Utah County.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal Riverton property taxes?
faqs.a: The Salt Lake County Board of Equalization accepts appeals from August 1 through September 15. The deadline is 45 days from the notice or September 15, whichever is longer.

faqs.q: When are Riverton property taxes due?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County says taxes are due November 30, whether or not you have received an appeal decision.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Riverton house with an unpermitted basement apartment?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as they are. Riverton regulates accessory dwellings through an application and owner-occupancy affidavit, so a conventional buyer might ask for proof the unit was approved. A cash sale avoids that step.
Riverton is in the Jordan School District. Many students attend schools in neighboring cities because attendance boundaries do not match the city limits.
